newsitem.title: USA: Genzyme Transgenics, Fresenius in pact.
newsitem.headline: Genzyme Transgenics, Fresenius in pact.

text.p: Genzyme Transgenics Corp said on Thursday it signed a transgenic commercialization agreement with Germany's Fresenius AG to develop and commercialize transgenic human serum albumin.
Albumin is a key protein involved in maintaining the balance of fluids in the blood.
To produce mass quantities of albumin, a human gene would be injected into the embryo of a cow. When the cow was full-grown, it would produce that protein in its milk, the company said.
Under the agreement, Fresenius AG would make initial, milestone, development and option payments totaling $17 million, Genzyme Transgenics said.
Upon product approval, Genzyme Transgenics said it would provide albumin to Fresenius at a transfer price and receive royalties on final product sales.
Fresenius would conduct clinical trials, register the product for sale, and market and distribute the transgenic albumin, the company said.
Albumin regulates the transport of amino acids, fatty acids, hormones, drugs, and drug metabolites.
